input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
input.rationale: § 8.2 auto-renews each Order Form for twelve months but requires one hundred eighty days' advance notice to stop renewal. That window exceeds both the fallback ceiling (60 days) and the 90-day walk-away threshold, so it is a material deviation. The renewal term itself (twelve months) is acceptable, and § 8.3 already caps uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, which satisfies the price element at both levels. We therefore target the fallback with the single smallest change: reduce the non-renewal notice window to sixty days. The absence of a Vendor renewal reminder and the thirty-day preferred window are noted only as short of preferred, not flagged.

mappings.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
mappings.quote: On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A one-hundred-eighty-day non-renewal window is beyond our walk-away threshold, so we have shortened it to sixty days, which is our fallback position (our preferred window is thirty days). The renewal term and the CPI/three percent uplift cap in § 8.3 are unchanged.
proposal.summary: Shorten the Order Form non-renewal notice window from 180 days to 60 days.
